Q: What is the current status of Web Speech API's Recognition on Firefox / Gecko? A:

It seems like it was never fully implemented. However, as of January 2025 Firefox has officially indicated they are "Positive" about implementing the "Web Speech API".

“We believe this is a strong and welcome improvement to the API, on multiple aspects: added capabilities to the platform, in terms for feature and performance (e.g. being able to do high-quality low-latency recognition), but also accessibility and privacy.”

The GitHub Issue that triggered that change: GitHub: On-device Web Speech API

“This is positive and we're actively investigating, initially focusing on the recognition side of things.”

I cannot find a timeline of when this will come to Firefox—it is long overdue. However, a "positive" position usually means Firefox plans to implement the API in Firefox.

In fact, the entry in "Mozilla's Standards Positions" has a brand new bug ticket connected to it: Bugzilla: Implement on-device Web Speech Recognition. That bug is currently marked with P2 priority (ranges from P1 to P5), which means:

“We want this, but it's not totally clear or extremely important.”

The full list of Mozilla's positions on standards and proposed standards can be found here: https://mozilla.github.io/standards-positions/#web-speech-api-on-device

Q: How to respond to format from form post parameters A:

If you just ensure that the select actually has the attribute name="format" it will work exactly as intended as ActionDispatch::Http::MimeNegotiation.formats uses the merged parameters:

module ActionDispatch
  module Http
    module MimeNegotiation
      # ...
      def formats
        fetch_header("action_dispatch.request.formats") do |k|
          v = if params_readable?
            Array(Mime[parameters[:format]])
          elsif use_accept_header && valid_accept_header
            accepts.dup
          elsif extension_format = format_from_path_extension
            [extension_format]
          elsif xhr?
            [Mime[:js]]
          else
            [Mime[:html]]
          end

          v.select! do |format|
            format.symbol || format.ref == "*/*"
          end

          set_header k, v
        end
      end

If that's not possible you can overwrite request.format on the controller level by using the format= method:

class ApplicationController < ActionController::Base
  before_action :override_format, if: -> { params.dig(:form, :format).present? }

  def override_format
    request.format = params[:form][:format]
  end
end

Q: Get IP address of KVM Guest vm A:

virsh domifaddr examples

Example outputs with static IP's, one VM running, having two network interfaces, each on a different IPv4 network:

# Get vm name(s):

$ virsh list
 Id   Name           State
--------------------------------
 46   your-vm-name   running

# Get static IP's (NOT assigned by DHCP):

$ virsh domifaddr your-vm-name --source arp
 Name       MAC address          Protocol     Address
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 vnet84     52:54:00:e6:f0:87    ipv4         192.168.122.10/0

# Get dynamic IP's (assigned by DHCP):

$ virsh domifaddr your-vm-name --source lease
 Name       MAC address          Protocol     Address
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Get even more IP's:

$ virsh domifaddr your-vm-name --source agent
 Name       MAC address          Protocol     Address
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 lo         00:00:00:00:00:00    ipv4         127.0.0.1/8
 -          -                    ipv6         ::1/128
 enp1s0     52:54:00:e6:f0:87    ipv4         192.168.122.10/24
 -          -                    ipv6         fe80::5054:ff:fee6:f087/64
 enp2s0     52:54:00:b2:3f:82    ipv4         192.168.125.10/24
 -          -                    ipv6         fe80::5054:ff:feb2:3f82/64

These commands can then be combined with grep, head and/or awk to meet the needs of using the IP's in a bash script.

Q: disable editing in cells without protecting worksheet vba A:

I had a similar issue and found a workaround. For whatever reason I couldn't get my macros to run correctly with the sheets protected so what I did is as a code to Pop up a message box for any cells that I didn't want the user to change. Then I added "Application.DisplayAlerts = False" to the beginning of any codes that needed to modify those cells and reset the alerts back to True at the end of those codes.

Q: How to indent bullet in PowerPoint VBA A:

You are seeing that extra space because you have chr(9) in your original code and that is a Tab character. So try vbCrLf (which is carriage return followed by line feed) instead of the chr(13) & chr(9).

.TextFrame.TextRange.Text = "1" & vbCrLf & "2" & vbCrLf & "3" & vbCrLf & "4"

Q: Exception while connecting to DB2 in java using JDBC A:

Your first two attempts were not supposed to work. You're using the JCC driver URL format, so it wouldn't be valid for either "net" or "app" drivers, which are deprecated anyway.

Use the JCC driver (com.ibm.db2.jcc.DB2Driver) and the URL format of "jdbc:db2://hostname:portnumber/databasename" and see this technote for the solution to the "Security mechanism not supported" problem. In short, you need to use a supported JDK.

Q: "turtle" package could not be installed for Python 3 using pip A:

You don't need to install turtle at all.

The turtle graphics library built on top of python-tk is part of the Python 3 standard library. It doesn't require installation; it's already included with Python 3.

The thing pip is trying to install is a much older library with the same name but built for a completely different purpose, which was never updated to be compatible with Python 3 in the first place.

Just import turtle. You don't need to install anything first.

(That said, note that you need python3-tk, not python-tk, to use turtle with Python 3).

To demonstrate the above, see the file list for libpython3.10-stdlib for the Jammy release of Ubuntu (amd64); you'll see /usr/lib/python3.10/turtle.py included.
